A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoNCE population-geometry research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between appendices.

before.justification: v3 Section 5 and Appendix E report original synthetic experiments, particle simulations, pretrained OpenCLIP analyses, and controlled MS-COCO caption-corruption experiments.

after.justification: v7 Section 5 and Appendix F retain these original experimental and simulation results.

M1.justification: The InfoNCE and symmetric CLIP objectives, encoder constructions, and particle/KDE optimization procedures remain unchanged. Revised mathematical domains and terminology concern the analysis rather than a new learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture gradient experiment, two-well spherical simulation, latent-angle misalignment scenario, and MS-COCO pretrained-model and caption-corruption studies.

E2.justification: The Gibbs and large-batch references remain unchanged. Table 2 retains the same nine OpenCLIP checkpoints, and the corruption experiment retains ResNet-50 and ViT-B-16. Newly cited related work is not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Matched experimental settings remain unchanged, including the 4,096-negative reference pool, temperature and misalignment sweeps, first 5,000 COCO validation images with up to five captions each, and projection-head fine-tuning with batch size 256 for 5,000 steps.

E4.justification: The negative-count, temperature, misalignment, and caption-corruption analyses are retained, together with polar marginals, joint-angle heatmaps, residual-angle distributions, and retrieval-versus-gap comparisons. Their questions and displayed evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20-seed synthetic experiments, standard deviations for gradient diagnostics, and standard errors for concentration and marginal-gap summaries. The qualitative misalignment plots still use representative seed 0.

E6.justification: Table 2 values, plotted experimental results, and caption-corruption scores are unchanged. A limited qualitative finding is narrowed: v3 Appendix E.3 describes residual angle-shift distributions as having heavy tails, whereas v7 Appendix F.3 reports broadening without that characterization.

T1.justification: Definition 4.3 restricts the intrinsic multimodal problem to bounded potentials and essentially bounded densities, replacing the earlier general floored L1 class. Appendix D.2 replaces an unsupported absolute-continuity rate argument with a bounded-density estimate. Corollary E.2 adds a uniform positive lower bound on excess mass absent from Corollary B.2. Large-batch proofs also correct derivative handling and justify expectation limits explicitly.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions remain substantially intact. However, the introduction replaces generic modality-gap and knife-edge matching assertions with the narrower claim that incompatible directional structures can sustain separation, and more precisely confines convexity to the intrinsic geometry.

C2.justification: V7 systematically distinguishes pointwise objective/gradient consistency from training trajectories, and coordinate infima from attained best responses. It withdraws v3's assertions that misalignment necessarily forces separation that optimization cannot remove. Experimental discussion now treats the retained observations as controlled illustrations and particle-surrogate agreement, with more restrained causal and equilibrium interpretations.

D1.justification: The first-page footnote replaces the project-page reference with explicit code-repository access information and archival citation guidance. Experimental implementation details and hyperparameters remain substantially unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish when the code became available.

R1.justification: V7 adds Betser et al. (2025, 2026), Levi and Gilboa (2025), and Yi et al. (2025), including discussion of conditions permitting gap-closing optima. It removes the Liu–Wang and Welling–Teh particle-method citations. The Arora (2019) to Saunshi (2019) citation change identifies the same work.

P1.justification: Main-text explanations, proof intuitions, related work, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Terminology and notation are standardized. Former Appendices B.3–B.4 become E.1–E.2, experiments move from E to F, discussion moves from F to G, and a changelog is added.

P2.justification: The main paper switches from two columns to a single-column preprint layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, a new geometry schematic becomes Figure 2, and the earlier Figures 2 and 3 are combined into four-panel Figure 3. Figures and tables are resized or relocated while retaining their experimental data.

improvement.justification: For this primarily theoretical paper, repairing support for central results is a substantial gain: Definition 4.3 and Appendix D.2 replace an unjustified limiting argument with a bounded-density proof, while Corollary E.2 supplies a missing nondegeneracy condition. More careful claims also resolve discrepancies between the proven limits and earlier trajectory or inevitability language. Applicability is narrower, and minor notation errors are introduced, including missing grouping in Corollary E.2's excess-density definition, but the surrounding decomposition makes the intended expression recoverable.
